Model-based digital pianos: from physics to sound synthesis

Concert-grand pp/mf/ff timbre fit and unused check pitches

provenance.notes: Tuning, inharmonicity, and base string loss use the earlier mf/ff fit at C2, C3, Gb3, C4, C5, Eb5, C6, A6, and C7. Low-bass loss blends into the modeled A0 values; upper values use the C7 anchor. The three shared felt centers use attack residuals from those notes. Hammer contact, filtering, shared bridge loss, and broad per-key radiation EQ now use onset-aligned Iowa pp/mf/ff spectra and partial envelopes at C2 through C7, with G3/G4/G5 reserved for checks. The six anchor values interpolate across keys and clamp beyond their range. Velocity-to-hardness scaling remains modeled. This fit measures note spectra, including room and microphone color, not isolated soundboard response or hammer speed. Choir levels, unison width, felt register terms, the body modes and coupling matrix, short bridge response, FDN, dampers, pedal travel, sympathetic bank, and mechanical sounds remain modeled. See fit/concert-grand-timbre.json for targets, fit steps, and limits.
